# Fasting vs. calorie restriction for weight loss: Which one wins?
## News briefs
If you're tired of counting calories to lose weight, you might consider a style of intermittent fasting called 4:3. It allows you to eat normally on four days of the week, and eat very little (fast) on the other three days, which can be spread throughout the week.
This approach might even help you lose more weight than counting calories, notes a small randomized controlled trial published in the May 20, 2025, issue of _Annals of Internal Medicine_ .

answer:
Yes. Intermittent fasting can lead to somewhat more weight loss than daily calorie restriction.

A randomized trial of 165 people in the May 20, 2025 issue of Annals of Internal Medicine found that a 4:3 fasting plan produced about 6 more pounds of weight loss after one year than daily calorie reduction [1]. Another report of a 12-month trial in 165 adults states that the 4:3 group lost 2.89 kg more than the daily-restriction group [2]. In that trial, fasting participants lost 7.6 percent of body weight, compared with 5.0 percent in the daily-restriction group [2].

A 2023 meta-analysis of seven randomized trials with 458 participants found that time-restricted eating plus a calorie deficit produced 2.11 kg more weight loss than calorie restriction alone [2]. A 2022 meta-analysis of 11 trials with 705 participants reported a small but statistically significant weight-loss advantage for fasting over continuous calorie restriction [2]. Another systematic review and meta-analysis concluded that intermittent fasting appears slightly advantageous over energy restriction for body weight, cardiometabolic factors, and plasma glucose levels [6]. One review of studies also suggests intermittent fasting may be superior to continuous calorie restriction for weight loss in some respects [5].
